title: Claude terminal 256-color renderer consistency review
scope: Shared xterm DOM/WebGL rendering of ANSI indexed colors emitted by Provider terminals

evidence.observation: The Claude replay contains ANSI 38;5; and 48;5; sequences, including index 208 (orange), while the desktop view exposes color mainly in code diffs.
evidence.risk: The PTY bytes are intact but the renderer or custom palette is collapsing indexed colors in ordinary terminal output.

evidence.observation: TerminalView uses one custom theme with WebGL and a DOM fallback for every Provider; no Provider-specific renderer exists.
evidence.risk: A renderer-level palette regression can affect Claude while simpler 16-color diff output appears healthy.

decision.renderer: Preserve xterm's complete ANSI indexed-color semantics when applying the shared theme, across WebGL and DOM fallback.
decision.verification: Add a focused regression that feeds representative 256-color SGR sequences and proves the terminal surface keeps distinct indexed foreground/background colors.

acceptance: Representative Claude-style 38;5; and 48;5; sequences remain distinct from the base foreground/background colors.
WebGL and DOM rendering use the same complete indexed-color palette and ordinary non-diff output retains color.
The fix remains Provider independent and does not strip or rewrite PTY bytes.
